```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

# The R code in this document is split up into different code chunks. Each chunk
# corresponds to one of the sections of the R script files we have created
# previously, e.g. one section to load the data, another to wrangle it, etc.
# Quarto files might need more chunks than there are sections in an R script
# file, because you will probably want to add text between different maps,
# tables, etc. in the output.
#
# Each code chunk in this document has a label at the start. This label will be
# used in any error messages produced when you render the document, making it
# easier to find the source of errors.

pacman::p_load(gt, here, httr2, janitor, sf, sfhotspot, tidyverse)
```

```{r}
#| label: load-data
#| cache: true
#| include: false

# Create the directory for the original downloaded data
dir.create(here("data", "raw"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Download the original data into the project
request(
  "https://mpjashby.github.io/crimemappingdata/medellin_homicides.csv"
) |>
  req_perform(path = here("data", "raw", "medellin_homicides.csv"))

request(
  "https://mpjashby.github.io/crimemappingdata/medellin_comunas.gpkg"
) |>
  req_perform(path = here("data", "raw", "medellin_comunas.gpkg"))

# Load homicide data from the local copy
homicides <- read_csv2(here("data", "raw", "medellin_homicides.csv")) |>
  janitor::clean_names() |>
  drop_na(longitud, latitud) |>
  st_as_sf(coords = c("longitud", "latitud"), crs = "EPSG:4326") |>
  st_transform("EPSG:3115")

# Load neighbourhood boundaries from the local copy
medellin_comunas <- read_sf(
  here("data", "raw", "medellin_comunas.gpkg")
) |>
  janitor::clean_names() |>
  st_transform("EPSG:3115") |>
  select(nombre, geom) |>
  mutate(nombre = str_to_title(nombre))
```

```{r}
#| label: wrangle-data
#| include: false

# Count homicides in each neighbourhood separately for each year
homicide_count <- homicides |>
  mutate(year = lubridate::year(fecha_hecho)) |>
  group_by(year) |>
  # `.x` contains the homicide points for one year
  group_modify(~ hotspot_count(.x, grid = medellin_comunas)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  # `group_modify()` returns a tibble; restore its spatial class before
  # removing geometry for the table
  st_as_sf() |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  select(nombre, year, n) |>
  # Include years with no homicides anywhere in the city as well
  complete(
    nombre = medellin_comunas$nombre,
    year = 2010:2019,
    fill = list(n = 0)
  )

# Convert that data into a format that is suitable for displaying in a table
homicide_table <- homicide_count |>
  # Calculate the mean number of homicides in each neighbourhood per year
  group_by(nombre) |>
  mutate(mean_count = mean(n)) |>
  # Arrange the neighbourhoods by mean count of homicides in descending order
  arrange(desc(mean_count)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  # Convert the data to wide format for easier display
  pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = n, values_fill = 0)

# The next piece of code uses the `pull()` function from the dplyr package to
# extract columns from datasets (e.g. so they can be summarised using functions
# such as `max()`) and the `pluck()` function from the purrr package to extract
# single values from datasets. It also uses functions from the scales package to
# format values so that they are easier to read.
```

@tbl-homicide-counts shows the number of homicides in each neighbourhood of Medellín in each year from `r min(pull(homicide_count, "year"))` to `r max(pull(homicide_count, "year"))`. During that time, on average the `r pluck(homicide_table, "nombre", 1)` neighbourhood had the highest number of homicides (`r scales::comma(pluck(homicide_table, "mean_count", 1), accuracy = 1)` per year).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-homicide-counts
#| tbl-cap: "Homicides in neighbourhoods of Medellín"

homicide_table |>
  # Remove columns we don't want to include in the table
  select(-mean_count) |>
  # Use neighbourhood names as row labels and format whole-number counts
  gt(rowname_col = "nombre") |>
  fmt_number(columns = where(is.numeric), decimals = 0)
```
